[the rule's own record before the fold]
kb/Work PB110 (2026-08-19): a) a name defined once across the paragraph's SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS clauses (COBOL1670); b)/c) positional pairing, one-to-one (1670 — the negative pins two names against one integer); d) ALPHANUMERIC implied; e)/f) the ordinal shall exist in the native set of the clause's class or the IN alphabet's set, which shall be of that class (1670, the range and class-mismatch arms); g) alphabet-name-3 shall not be a LOCALE alphabet — COBOL1669 through the ONE coded-set resolver (the negative).

[folded SR-12.3.7.3-L4.1 = §12.3.7.3 16) e) 1.: CONFORMS]
kb/Work PB1091: SR16 e)1 (cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 'When the IN phrase is specified, alphabet-name-3 shall reference an alphabet that defines an alphanumeric character set, and the ordinal position specified by integer-1 shall exist in that character set.' -> OK 16) 1.). The class of the IN alphabet is compared with the clause's, and the ordinal is read by the one reader, so 129 and 99999999999 IN STANDARD-1 are refused under SR16 e1 (the silent int.TryParse skip is gone); 128 IN STANDARD-1 defines the character.

[folded SR-12.3.7.3-L4.2 = §12.3.7.3 16) e) 2.: CONFORMS]
kb/Work PB1091: SR16 e)2 (cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 'When the IN phrase is not specified, the ordinal position specified by integer-1 shall exist in the native alphanumeric character set.' -> OK 16) 2.). The native alphanumeric set is the 65,536 UTF-16 code units (DOC-A.1-188). An ordinal outside 1..65536 at ANY magnitude draws COBOL1670 naming SR16 e2 on the clause (SA1/SA15 used to compile clean), and the name stays DEFINED so its first use draws no second, false 'not defined' diagnostic.

[folded SR-12.3.7.3-L5.1 = §12.3.7.3 16) f) 1.: CONFORMS]
kb/Work PB1091: SR16 f)1 (cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 'When the IN phrase is specified, alphabet-name-3 shall reference an alphabet that defines a national character set, and the ordinal position specified by integer-1 shall exist in that character set.' -> OK 16) 1.). The class half compares the IN alphabet with FOR NATIONAL; the ordinal half (UCS-4 has 1,112,064 scalar values) is read by the one reader, so 1112065 and 4294967297 IN a UCS-4 alphabet are refused under SR16 f1 and 1112064 defines the character.

[folded SR-12.3.7.3-L5.2 = §12.3.7.3 16) f) 2.: CONFORMS]
kb/Work PB1091: two rules. (1) SR16 f)2 (cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 'When the IN phrase is not specified, the ordinal position specified by integer-1 shall exist in the native national character set.' -> OK 16) 2.): the native national set is 65,536 code units; an ordinal outside 1..65536 at any magnitude is refused under SR16 f2 (SA16 used to compile clean). (2) SR16 g) (cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 'Alphabet-name-3 shall not reference an alphabet specified with the LOCALE phrase.' -> OK 16) g)) is enforced by the one resolver CodedCharacterSetOf (pb110-symbolic-locale-alphabet); the undeclared-IN-name message quality is kb/Work PB789's.
